notes:
Account brief: ShelfWave Retain is a mid-market SaaS (B2B knowledge management) that powers customer-facing KB search and in-app assistants for ~200 customers. Primary pain: search relevance + cost at scale. They plan to index ~3-7M doc chunks (many small fragments from KB, articles, release notes).

Key technical requirements:
- Workload: high QPS retrieval + lightweight neural rerank on top (embedding-based ann -> small cross-encoder reranker for top-K).
- QPS targets: sustained 150-250 QPS normal, burst to 500 QPS during peak.
- Latency SLOs: first-pass ANN <= 80ms median, rerank end-to-end <= 250ms p95 ideally. Current POC p95 ~320ms (rerank CPU-bound).
- Cost sensitivity: target effective cost per user query < $0.003 (hosted) including embeddings + rerank compute; strong interest in batching/caching and quantized model recommendations.
- Indexing: incremental daily ingest of ~50k docs, cold-start backfill ~5M chunks; vector dim preference 1536 or 1024 (ok to tune).
- Models: prefer Llama-2 style open quantized for rerank if accuracy acceptable; open to Redwood-verified rerank variants.
- Security: SSO (SAML), audit logging, customer KMS support, and EU data residency for subset of customers.

Quotes from stakeholders:
- Head of Product: "We need rewrites in results to drop false positives — reranker must explain why it demoted hits."
- Engineering manager: "Cost/latency tradeoff is the blocker; if we can get p95 under 250ms we can go GA."
